14233.title: Released binaries have High severity CVEs due to Go version 1.24.1
14233.feasibility_reason: The issue points directly to upgrading the Go toolchain version in the Dockerfile and go.mod to resolve high severity CVEs in standard library dependencies.
14233.problem_summary: Prebuilt binaries contain high-severity standard library vulnerabilities (e.g., in crypto/tls, os, net/url, and archive/zip) because they were compiled using an outdated Go toolchain version.
14233.root_cause_hypothesis: The Go version pinned in go.mod, Dockerfile, and CI/release workflows specifies a Go release with known standard library vulnerabilities.
14233.suggested_approach: Upgrade the Go toolchain directive in go.mod, Dockerfile, and GitHub Actions workflow files to a patched Go release that resolves the reported CVEs.
prerequisites: Installed Go toolchain matching the target updated version
implementation_steps: Update the `go` and/or `toolchain` directives in `go.mod` to the target patched Go version.
Update any Go version references or base image tags in `Dockerfile`.
Update the Go version specified in GitHub Actions CI and release workflow files under `.github/workflows/` (e.g., `actions/setup-go` step configurations).
Run `go mod tidy` and build the binary locally using the updated Go toolchain.
Run `govulncheck -mode=binary bin/ollama` (or on the compiled target) to verify that all standard library vulnerabilities have been resolved.
Execute test suites (`go test ./...`) to ensure compatibility and lack of regressions with the updated Go version.

15669.title: Both `qwen3.5:35b-a3b-coding-bf16` and `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-coding-bf16` are labeled as non-MLX, yet they are meant for macOS only
15669.feasibility_reason: The issue involves updating metadata or model tags in a model registry or configuration file where specific models are incorrectly flagged or filtered regarding platform requirements (macOS/MLX). This is a localized and straightforward fix.
15669.problem_summary: Users on Linux/Windows receive HTTP 412 'this model requires macOS' when attempting to pull certain non-MLX model tags (such as Qwen and Gemma variants) from the Ollama model registry.
15669.root_cause_hypothesis: The model registry manifests or server-side model routing metadata incorrectly tagged these specific model quantization/variant tags with an Apple Silicon/macOS runtime constraint (e.g. MLX format requirement or OS metadata check) instead of standard GGUF multi-platform compatibility, or the manifest distribution pipeline misclassified the model architecture tags during indexing.
15669.suggested_approach: Audit and correct the tag metadata and manifest manifests in the model library registry backend for the affected model tags, and verify/update client-side manifest compatibility checking logic to ensure non-MLX/standard GGUF models are not gated on macOS.
likely_areas: ollama/ollama model registry / backend manifest database
prerequisites: Access to the model catalog/registry metadata management tools and build pipelines
Test environments on both Linux and macOS to verify model manifest downloads and pull behavior
implementation_steps: Identify all affected model tags in the registry (e.g., qwen3.5:35b-a3b-coding-bf16, qwen3.6:35b-a3b-coding-bf16, nvfp4/mxfp8 tags, gemma4 tags).
Inspect the manifest descriptors and headers returned by the registry server for these tags to check if the 'os' or platform requirement fields are erroneously set to 'darwin' or 'mlx'.
Fix the backend model registry tagging / manifest generation pipeline so that standard GGUF weights are marked as platform-independent (or include linux/amd64 and windows/amd64).

Inspect client-side pull handling in Ollama codebase (e.g., in server/download.go and manifest parsing) to ensure platform requirement errors are descriptive and that valid cross-platform manifests are properly requested.
Republish/re-index the corrected manifests in the Ollama registry.
Verify using `ollama pull` on Linux x86_64/Nvidia machines to ensure the models download and run without HTTP 412 errors.
